name: Louis C.K.
note: STAGE PERSONA graph. All fields describe the performer-as-acted, never the private person. No verbatim set text stored here — transcripts live in theory/scribe/ and link by path. Fingerprints ≤7 words. Measured fields carry provenance; everything else is authored hypothesis until n>=3 sets.

identity.deal: Self-flagellating Everyman who walks his worst thoughts past every social stop sign until the room admits it shares them.
identity.premise: A bad person telling the truth about being bad until the audience recognizes itself.
identity.awareness_note: Head: aware failings = neurotic comedy. He KNOWS the thoughts are ugly; the telling is the transgression, and the knowing is what makes it bearable.

philosophy.ontology: Humans are animals in a thin coat of civilization, and the coat keeps slipping.
philosophy.epistemology: The thought you're ashamed of is the truest one you had.
philosophy.axiology: Honesty beats decency; the confession is the moral act even when the content isn't.
philosophy.causality: Civilization is a mass agreement not to say the thing; comedy breaks the agreement one room at a time.
philosophy.agency: One person saying the quiet part gives a room permission to feel less alone with it.

dramatic_core.want: the recognition laugh — I'm not the only one
dramatic_core.fear: being the only one who thinks it
dramatic_core.need: one more confession that lands harder than the last
dramatic_core.self_model: a decent man trapped in an indecent mind

identity.misinterpretation_rule: Treats his own worst impulse as universal law and keeps walking it until the room admits complicity.
contradictions: preaches empathy from a confessed position of terribleness
the confessional booth and its prosecutor in one body
claims loss of control while engineering every beat of the collapse

identity.style_thesis: Sincere-storyteller engine: treats his own worst impulse as universal law and keeps walking it until the room admits complicity. Content-valence and delivery-valence are OPPOSITE — the text reads like shame, the delivery is manic. That split is the engine.

engine.archetype_def: self-deprecating, takes audience to weird dark places; sincerity IS the engine; laughs are byproduct not target
engine.archetype_delivery: mid pitch, wide dynamics, build-then-collapse structure, physical specificity, comfort with silence

mary_coords.note: measured dominant modulator across roadrage stencil (11/12 segments manic). MARY via arxiv 2307.02132.

jev_state.finding: Jev predicts deadpan/embarrassed from text; ground truth is manic. The text sounds like shame, the delivery is energized. Content-valence and delivery-valence are OPPOSITE — this is the engine, and the model can't see it yet.

world_transfer_proven.note: His engine successfully delivered non-Louis material through his delivery contract. Material swappable; delivery is the constant.

sets.title: Road Rage (window 120-240s)
sets.status: partial — 2-minute window of a longer bit

timing_measured.thesis: fast speech, many pauses. 14 topic-pauses (>0.8s) are the confession holds. The two longest holds (8.16s, 5.32s) sit at the two darkest turns. Timing gates the laugh (DPV): the room needs the silence to catch up to what he just said about itself.

topics.why_it_works: Opens on universal fear (memory loss) stated as plain fact, no joke framing. The premise is real before it's funny — audience registers honesty first, which buys him the transgressions later.

Fonzie name-drop fails as shared reference — the joke is that HE can't remember, not that we should. Self-targeting via cultural literacy collapse. Micro-punches (1.32s, 1.48s holds) practice the pause grammar before the big holds.

Classic Louis escalation: a real-feeling mundane entry (guy in a van), increasingly absurd compliance, and the turn arrives when he admits the act wasn't even enjoyable. The 8.16s hold after b13 is the longest silence in the window — the room metabolizes the whole story in that gap. Confessional premise + absurd content = the signature collision.

Shifts from storytelling to live intrusive thought — the beautiful couple, the hidden child, the thought he shouldn't have. 5.32s hold after b16 is the second-longest. He never resolves it; the discomfort IS the payload. Awareness of the thought's ugliness is stated before the room can reject it.

The closer drops the story entirely and confesses the mechanism: he says terrible things because the audience's upset is enjoyable to him. This is the set's real thesis — the whole preceding transgression was a delivery vehicle for this admission. Audience laughs because it's true of comedy itself.

gtvh.note: premise beat; confessional open, no punch expected

interpretations.claim: 2.26s hold after a mortality statement — temporal scaffolding tells the room this is real before it's funny.
Premise delivered in one clean sentence. No smuggled laughs yet — the premise clarity doctrine (Rock quote in louistheory1) fully honored.
Content valence negative (death); delivery valence likely positive (manic per stencil seg0). The split starts immediately.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: worry about getting old only because

interpretations.claim: Second premise sentence narrows the fear from death to memory — the specific fear the whole bit will exploit.
garden_path: the 'only because' promises a surprising reason, delivers a smaller-than-expected one (memory, not death).

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: some of it I would love to lose

interpretations.claim: First smuggled micro-surprise inside the premise (louistheory1 pattern): the 'some of it' twist gets its own 1.88s beat.
double_interpret: 'lose my memory' as tragedy vs. as wish. Same words, two scripts.
rigidify: applies the literal rule of memory (all or none) to the wish. The bit's engine is taking a metaphor literally.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: take it all or none, I guess

interpretations.claim: Bridge from philosophical setup into the anecdote machine. Fonzie reference sets up a shared-cultural expectation that b05-b06 will collapse.
4-word punch after 0.78s setup — micro-punch. Practices the pause grammar at small scale before the 8s hold.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: don't even know what you're talking

interpretations.claim: Tag on b05: escalates from personal forgetting to attacking the audience's reference. split_knowledge — the room knows Fonzie; the persona doesn't.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: I forget weird things, you know

interpretations.claim: Anecdote entry. The van premise is delivered flat and real-feeling — the mundane doorway into the transgressive. 44 words with only inter-phrase pauses, then 2.04s hold before compliance.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: I said, all right, you know

interpretations.claim: The compliance beat — he accepts the absurd invitation with a shrug. This is the Everyman engine: the room would also say 'all right' in the bit's logic.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: got in the van and you know

interpretations.claim: Longest setup stretch (45w) ends in 2.86s hold — the physical-comedy beat (sliding door) gets a substantial pause as punctuation, not a punch.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: kneeling on the floor of the van

interpretations.claim: Physical absurdity (kneeling on a purse) against the transgressive frame. Stencil seg here is manic — the energy rides the escalation, never flinches.
The bluntest line in the window. character_violation fires — the social stop sign is named and walked past in the same breath. 1.40s hold lets the room catch up.
'I'm guessing' — faux-uncertainty marker that sets up the turn. 1.98s hold is the windup for the longest pause in the set.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: remembered that I don't really like

interpretations.claim: THE central beat. 8.16s hold — topic pause squared. The confession ('I don't really like doing that') arrives mid-act, reframes the whole story from transgression to boredom, and the silence is the room metabolizing both readings at once. DPV: temporal scaffolding OUTRANKS the semantic content here — the pause is doing more comedic work than the words.
Content is deflationary (boredom), delivery stays in the established manic frame — the mismatch after an 8s silence is where the laugh lands.
'Stay in the bit' (Jerry's rule from louistheory1): he doesn't break to acknowledge the huge laugh/silence; the next beat starts clean.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: looking at the couple and they're walking

interpretations.claim: Post-hold restart. New scene (the couple), new escalation axis (intrusive thought rather than action). Only 0.50s pause after — he rushes INTO the darkest section, no breathing room granted.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: I just see like a little head

interpretations.claim: figure_ground: the hidden child (ground) becomes the obsessive focus (figure). Perception filter made literal — attention goes where it shouldn't.

beat_decomposition.fingerprint: curious what their kid looks like

interpretations.claim: Second-longest hold (5.32s) after the thought the persona can't take back. The silence is the room deciding whether to laugh or leave; his stillness forces the laugh.
He names the ugly thought AS ugly ('I don't know') before the room can condemn it — pre-emptive self-indictment disarms moral objection.

The meta-confession closer. Drops the story, names the mechanism: he says terrible things because the room's upset is enjoyable to him. The whole van story was a delivery vehicle for this admission about comedy itself. This is why the engine transfers to any topic — the topic was never the point.
Audience and performer now share the same knowledge: we're all here for the transgression. The contract is spoken aloud, which is itself the final transgression.
'saying something terrible because it makes me laugh that it upsets you' — decent-man self-model colliding with cruel-entertainment want, in one sentence, unresolved. Engine fuel.

essay_seeds.title: The Eight-Second Confession: how Louis C.K. uses silence to make a room agree with him
essay_seeds.thesis: On a 2-minute window of Road Rage, the two longest pauses (8.16s, 5.32s) sit exactly at the two darkest semantic turns. Timing, not content, is doing the heaviest comedic work — the DPV claim (temporal scaffolding outranks incongruity) made flesh.
outline: what he said before the silence
the second hold as proof of pattern
why this is his engine and not an accident
what this means for the comedy-is-timing folk theory

essay_seeds.title: Sincerity as a delivery contract: why the model thinks Louis is sad and the room knows he's energized
essay_seeds.thesis: Jev's delivery decoder scores 0.19 emotion accuracy on Louis — it predicts deadpan/embarrassed from the text while ground-truth acoustic GT is 11/12 manic. The text reads like shame; the delivery is high-arousal positive-valence. That content/delivery valence split is the engine, and it's why text-only models fail on him.
outline: what the model sees in the words
the split as feature not bug
implication: comedy models need the delivery channel

essay_seeds.title: Against the joke: Louis C.K. and the comedy of the confession that isn't a joke
essay_seeds.thesis: The closer of Road Rage drops punchline logic entirely and states the mechanism ('saying something terrible because it upsets you'). Compared with Norm's insistence that every bit has a real punchline (normtheory1), Louis's late-period engine sometimes REPLACES the punchline with a confession about joke-telling. Both work; they're opposite doctrines.
outline: why each is consistent with its persona
what this says about two theories of why we laugh
predictions for other comics on this axis
